lens: STORY & CURIOSITY: arc, stakes, emotion, pacing across the whole runtime, memorable images, questions planted and paid off
method: Read all 182 narration lines (script.json), the timeline (24:15, 103 shots), qa/reports/latest.json, score/cues.json, story/reviews/round-3-story-editor.json, and contact sheets ch01-s01, s05, s06, s07, s08, ch02-s01, s03, s05, ch03-s06, ch04-s03, s06, s09, s10, s13, ch05-s01, s05, ch06-s02, s03, s10, s12, ch07-s02, s06, ch08-s02, s06, ch09-s06, s07, ch10-s02, ch11-s04, ch12-s03, s05, s06, s07. Round 1: no earlier reviews; film.json stages.fixes is empty, so there is no ledger to check. The story stage closed with pass:false (mean 7.9), and every round-3 story-editor issue I checked is still in the shipped narration word for word (L0605/L0615/L0625, L1101, L1207, L0813, L0423, L0608, L0613, L0617, L0412, L1007, L0206, L0305).
summary: A strong spine with real plants and payoffs. The 4.5 -> 11 cold open is a great hook, paid off three times (ch04-s06, ch04-s09, the HN stranger in ch10-s02). Kleene's finite machine pays off at ch06-s12 and ch09-s04, 'what is a GPU for?' at ch09-s03, the 1943 nets that could not learn at ch07-s03, and the finale's 'the struck ones ran too, multiplied by nought' rhymes with Deep Dive I. The film loses grip in three places. (1) Deep Dive II contradicts itself on one run per frame. (2) The second half drifts into a commit chronicle (ch08) with a silent plate nobody can decode, a flat chapter-out and a chronology slip into ch11. (3) The payoff of the 23-minute 'why?' tag rests on a quote lifted out of context. The tag-on-a-line device carries the story but uses four names (tags, guesses, promises, beliefs), and the strike gesture repeats so often that the second half feels like a ritual more than a discovery.

issues.problem: Deep Dive II undoes its own central mechanism. L0605 says 'The loom runs once'. L0615 strikes that ('a busy drag frame runs about seventeen'). Then L0625 brings it back as the lab's verdict ('One frame is one evaluation of a fixed-depth circuit'). The viewer leaves the host-loop deep dive unsure whether a frame is one pass or seventeen. The round-3 story review flagged this as critical, and it was never applied.
issues.fix: L0605: 'Inputs in. The loom runs. Next state copied back. The page moves.' L0615: '...Now a busy drag frame runs about seventeen: one for each move, at its own time, each a whole pass.' L0625: 'Each run is what the lab's guide calls “a fixed-depth circuit”. The host turns the crank as often as it likes. The circuit never stops early.' Re-anchor the ch06-s12 'repo' beat to 'circuit'.

issues.problem: The film plants a blank 'why would anyone build it this way?' tag at 0:50 (L0107a) and re-raises it at 21:00 (L1006, 'We'll keep it for the end'). The payoff then quotes the README's 'for fun', which there qualifies the choice of backend (JS or WebGPU), not the project. It also repeats 'Let's find out!' from L0702. The film's longest-running question pays off on a context shift.
issues.fix: Answer the why tag with what the repo actually says, in its own context. For example: 'To the stranger's “why?”, the README answers with a question of its own: “what does that even do? Let's find out!”' (the unfreezing line, Q-sourced). Or make the honest non-answer the payoff: the repo states no single reason, and the lab's open list is the answer. Drop 'for fun' unless it is quoted with its backend context.

issues.problem: Chronology slip at the moral climax. ch10 runs from 20 to 27 October, then ch11 opens 'One last experiment.' and the ear places it after Hacker News. It actually ran on 15-16 October. In a film about who believed what and when, this silent time-jump blurs 'the rule written first'.
issues.fix: L1101: 'Step back a week, to the two days after launch, and one last experiment. The search demo's JSON highlighter stops at the first mistake.' Keep the 'experiment' beat on 'experiment'.

issues.problem: ch08-s06 is a 9 s silent plate (3·v vs v·3 slope gauges, 'both ramps on their corners', 'fixed that morning · 274 tests pass'). Without a line, the viewer cannot tell what bug this is, why word order changed a gradient, or why it belongs to 'The Summer's Certainties'. It reads as an orphan between the checker story (ch08-s05) and the credits beat (ch08-s07).
issues.fix: Restore one short line over ch08-s06, about 12 words, for example: 'Even a slope can depend on word order: three times v, or v times three.' Keep the 'zero' beat on 'three times v'. Otherwise cut ch08-s06 and give its 9 s to ch08-s08's relight.

issues.problem: 'Fit columns in a window seventeen hundred and thirty-two pixels wide. Doubles fit seven; thirty-two-bit floats fall a hair short.' The stakes are never said aloud (a whole column disappears, columns >= 7: 0). It sits inside a three-shot FP32 digression (ch04-s12/s13/s14) that interrupts the 4.5 thread between 'Answer: eight' (ch04-s07) and 'The real library won't compare until you promise a range' (ch04-s08), so the ear loses the chapter's through-line.
issues.fix: Say the consequence: '...Doubles fit seven. Thirty-two-bit floats come out a hair short of seven, and the seventh column vanishes.' Also consider moving ch04-s12..s14 after ch04-s11 (the 'Sixteen against two' close), so the 4.5 promise thread runs unbroken from s07 to s11.

issues.problem: 'In mid-September, he settled three questions.' is the flattest chapter-out in the film, and it leads into the October climax. The three answers on the card are machines the viewer has already met (the index read, the comparison helper, JS writing the springs), but the voice never connects them.
issues.fix: 'In mid-September, he settled three questions, with three machines we've met: an index read, one comparison, and springs worked out ahead in JavaScript.'

issues.problem: 'the familiar loop drifts up to three hundred and fifty-nine pixels apart'. 'The familiar loop' is never defined, and the ear hears it as Handwired's clockwork from the shot before, which makes the comparison backwards.
issues.fix: 'Replay one session at two frame rates, and an ordinary animation loop drifts up to three hundred and fifty-nine pixels apart.'

issues.problem: 'at rest, it comes out moving' sounds like a riddle by ear: what is at rest, and what comes out of what?
issues.fix: 'One step multiplies two numbers, the window's distance from home and its speed. A window at rest, three hundred pixels out, comes out moving.'

issues.problem: 'add a huge odd number' plants a question the voice never answers. Why odd? The visual pays it off (hollow odd tick, filled even tick), but 'Ties go to the even side' leaves the ear to make the link.
issues.fix: L0424: 'Up there floats sit one apart, and ties round to the even one; the huge number is odd, so a half lands on the even side above it: one.' Or simplify to the one image the visual shows.

issues.problem: 'In pairs, then pairs of pairs: three or four.' By ear the narrator sounds unsure at the moment that should feel precise.
issues.fix: 'In pairs, then pairs of pairs: three steps deep, or four for the leaner tree.'

issues.problem: 'Past nearly seventeen million' contradicts itself (past, but nearly?).
issues.fix: 'Past about seventeen million (two to the twenty-fourth), floats skip whole numbers.'

issues.problem: 'the strangers' pencils were gentler than its own' rests on PJ28, which says only that no public discussion of the lab was found. The strangers did not judge the lab gently: they never judged it at all. It ends ch10 on a figure of speech the evidence doesn't hold up.
issues.fix: 'About the lab, we found no public word. Its harshest critic was itself.'

issues.problem: The opening history runs 1:42-3:12, and the first mechanism shot after the cold open arrives at 4:44. ch02-s04 (the 2020 human-neuron finding) is the one tag in ch02 that never pays off later. It costs 15 s of the brief's 'brief framing' budget and delays the first deep dive.
issues.fix: Cut L0208b and keep L0209 as a 6-7 s beat, or fold 'As biology, the logic-gate tag frayed' into ch02-s02. Give the time back to ch06-s10 (sort, 8.2 s, rushed) or to the new ch08-s06 line.

issues.problem: The film's one device goes by four names: tags (L0107), guesses (L0312, L0505), promises (L0113, L1004) and beliefs (L1109, L1201-L1202). By the finale the ear has to translate, which blunts the re-hang and the wave of light.
issues.fix: Settle on 'tag' as the object and 'promise' as what is written on it. Change L1201 to 'Every tag in the film hangs over the time it held.' and L1202 to 'Now re-hang the tags the way the loom does...'. Reword L1109 to 'This is how a tag should come down: by a rule written before the test.'

issues.problem: The sort-by-counting machine is one of the film's most memorable ideas ('Nothing swaps'), but the shot is 8.2 s and the sorted row 10 20 30 30 lands with about 1 s left. The payoff has no time to register.
issues.fix: Extend ch06-s10 by about 2 s of hold after the 'slide' beat (paid by trimming ch02-s04), so the cards settle and the ranks 2 0 3 1 -> slots read.

issues.problem: The tag-wall composition (a line of tags, a silhouette hand with a red pencil striking one) returns in ch01-s05, ch01-s07, ch02-s05, ch03-s06, ch08-s02, ch09-s07, ch10-s02, ch11-s04 and ch12. By the second half the strike is a ritual more than a discovery, and the tags are too small to read in wide frames (ch10-s02, ch09-s07).
issues.fix: Vary the strike's staging in the second half: a close-up on one tag, the struck tag falling onto the rule, or a strike seen only as a shadow. In wide tag-wall frames, push in to the two or three tags the line names.

issues.problem: QA stt fail: 'Lou' is heard as 'Lu' in L0301 and L0810. The author's name is the one human anchor the film has.
issues.fix: Add a lexicon entry for Cheng Lou (alias spelling 'Low') and re-narrate L0301 and L0810, then run film:stt.

best_moments: ch01-s06: the README's (a > 4) ? 10 : 12 built from two ramps and a lever; 4.5 gives 11 before the narrator says it. A cold-open hook that is real arithmetic.
ch04-s06: the dimmer switch: a = 4.5 -> 0.5x10 + 0.5x12 = 11, then a = 4.25 -> 11.5. The caveat becomes something you can see.
ch04-s10: the row of lenses magnifying by 2^149 until the faintest difference becomes a full bar; '16 OPS' against '2 OPS' makes 'one honest sentence about your input saves fourteen operations' land.
ch07-s03: 'The valve shuts, and every slope behind it goes dark', paid off with 'The neurons of 1943 couldn't learn. These can, if you let them.'
ch09-s06 -> s07: the RegExp face-off (2.1 s vs 11 ms), then 'That tag held for hours' and 'RegExp is fast.' The film's best reversal, humble and funny.
ch10-s02: a Hacker News stranger tries four and a half, 'you get 11', and the tag turns over to show the landing page already said so.
ch12-s03: one wave of light through the re-hung tags; 'The struck ones ran too. Multiplied by nought.' A thematic rhyme with both-branches-always-run.
ch12-s06: one hand passes a tag to an open palm on 'It's waiting for the next pair of hands.' A quiet, earned last image.
The silent X-ray desk device (ch03-s07, ch04-s16, ch05-s07, ch06-s13, ch07-s12) adds one component per chapter: a structural rhyme you feel more than you notice.
